messages:
Anya: Following up on the RFC — sketching an epoch-watermark + cooldown approach to reduce handoff thrash and make ownership transfers idempotent. TL;DR: attach an ownership_epoch and watermark to prefix leases, and reject rapid reclaims during a cooldown window. Thoughts?

Leo: Sounds promising. Curious how this interacts with prefetch: do we let in-flight prefetches finish if epoch changes?

Anya: Good call. Plan is: prefetches check epoch on completion; if epoch mismatches then they either commit to local KV but mark as tombstoned for replay, or drop and signal a read-repair. Prefer drop+read-repair to avoid cross-epoch contamination.

Sam: How would rejection look in practice? Need a clear contract for callers so we don't spin retries. Maybe return a dedicated error code like PREFIX_EPOCH_MISMATCH and include the current epoch and cooldown_remaining_ms.

Maria: +1 to explicit error. Also we should expose cooldown metrics so ops can see if cooloffs are causing tail latencies. eg prefix.cooldown.count and prefix.cooldown.ms_histogram.

Anya: Prototype config (example):

```
ownership_epoch: 12345
watermark_ts: 1769999900
cooldown_ms: 5000
handoff_policy: "graceful-drop"
```

Anya: Handoff flow idea: 1) new owner writes a claim with epoch+watermark; 2) old owner sees claim and starts demote; 3) for next cooldown_ms, any incoming writes that don't include matching epoch are either forwarded to new owner or rejected with PREFIX_EPOCH_MISMATCH.

Leo: Forwarding seems expensive on hot prefixes. Can we instead have a short pinned-forward window where the old owner proxies but doesn't prefetch? That keeps client latency but avoids rehydration churn.

Sam: Proxying works but we need backpressure protections. If old owner is overloaded during proxy window we should escalate to immediate failure so caller retries a routing layer. 

Maria: Regarding correctness: what about tombstone compaction? If we demote and compact tombstones before new owner finishes prefill we'll lose data. We must ensure compaction is gated by epoch: compact only tombstones with epoch < ownership_epoch.

Anya: Exactly. Compaction gating is part of design. Also thinking of keeping a tiny circular log of recent handoff events (epoch,id,watermark) for read-repair diagnostics. ops-bot can surface when clients hit mismatches.

ops-bot: New metric proposal recorded: prefix.epoch_mismatch.total and prefix.handoff.events(5m window). See <https://internal/reports/epoch-metrics>

Leo: Can we get a microbenchmark? Key invariants I'd like verified: no stale write wins after handoff, and bounded additional tail latency for first N requests post-handoff.

Anya: I'll spin up a spike that simulates hotkey handoffs under different cooldown_ms and proxy durations. Plan: run 1k QPS with variable prefetch, measure p50/p99 and mismatch rate.

Sam: Add a test for cross-node clock skew. If watermark_ts is clock-derived we need to tolerate small skews; prefer epoch monotonic counters instead of absolute ts for correctness.

Anya: Agreed — epoch is monotonic counter owned by orchestrator, watermark_ts only for observability. We'll add a monotonic epoch assignment in claim flow.

Maria: Action items: (1) Anya spike + report, (2) Leo to draft error/contract snippet for PREFIX_EPOCH_MISMATCH, (3) Sam to propose compaction-gating implementation, (4) ops-bot to wire the metrics.

Anya: I'll post spike results in eng-runtime channel in 2 days. If numbers look good we can fold into the next prefix-ownership refactor RFC and include a tiny migration plan for existing leases. :thumbsup:

Leo: One more note — we should avoid locking the lease table for long during claim processing. Use CAS on lease row with epoch check to keep it async-friendly.

Sam: I'll sketch CAS pseudo: `UPDATE leases SET epoch = new WHERE epoch = old AND lease_id = X` and if it fails retry with exponential backoff up to 20ms. Keep retries low to avoid thundering.

Maria: Sounds good. Thanks all.

Anya: Thanks — marking this thread as the implementation coordination point. I'll create a tracking ticket and link it to the RFC.
